facility: Enterprise Products Pascagoula Gas Plant, brazed aluminum heat exchanger rupture, fires and explosions, Pascagoula, Mississippi, June 27, 2016
source: U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board, Loss of Containment, Fires, and Explosions at Enterprise Products Midstream Gas Plant, Report No. 2016-02-I-MS, 2019 (public record)
question: On the night of June 27, 2016, while operators were curtailing and then shutting in NGL production on A-Train, a sudden explosion and fire destroyed much of the A-Train cryogenic area of the Pascagoula gas plant; 13 pieces of piping and equipment ruptured. Using the timeline, DCS data, physical evidence, the plant's brazed aluminum heat exchanger (BAHX) operating and repair history and the industry guidance, identify the most likely initial failure point and damage mechanism, explain how it led to a sudden rupture on that night, and recommend what the operator and industry should change (operation, monitoring, repair practice, mechanical integrity / risk assessment) to prevent a repeat.

criteria.name: BAHX rate-of-change limit - start-up / shutdown
criteria.source: p.32 Table 3 - ALPEMA / Chart / GPA Midstream / API 662 guidance
criteria.value: ROC no more than 3.6 degF (2 degC)/min during start-up or shutdown

criteria.name: BAHX total temperature change limit
criteria.source: p.32 Table 3 - ALPEMA / Chart / GPA guidance (API 662 No)
criteria.value: Total temperature change no more than 108 degF (60 degC) in an hour

criteria.name: BAHX cyclic operation suitability
criteria.source: p.41 - BP Group Practice GP-26-10 Guidance on Practice for Heat Exchangers
criteria.value: Advise against using BAHXs in service that experiences fluctuations in temperature / thermal cycling

criteria.name: PSM coverage
criteria.value: PGP is PSM-covered; requires PHA, operating procedures, MOC, mechanical integrity, incident investigation

criteria.name: RMP coverage
criteria.value: PGP is RMP-covered; requires hazard review and release prevention

criteria.name: Emergency response philosophy
criteria.value: Vent fuel to flare or vent to atmosphere and let fire burn to minimize vapor-cloud explosion extending offsite

criteria.name: Leak-before-break (LBB) use conditions
criteria.value: LBB only valid if crack growth rate low, leaking fluid not above auto-ignition / dangerous condition, in-service monitoring to detect leaks, and engineering calculation that leaking crack size < critical crack size

criteria.name: BAHX structural integrity criterion
criteria.source: p.15 Fig.5 discussion - brazed fin to cap/parting sheet joints act as truss
criteria.value: Fins and braze joints must hold layers together against fluid pressure; loss of braze / fatigue crack = loss of containment integrity

rfi.issue: Breach count conflict: task states 13 pieces ruptured vs p.62 states 12 breaches identified
rfi.item: Total count and identity of failed piping/equipment items
rfi.reason: Cannot close equipment-failure progression and consequence assessment without reconciled inventory
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION with reason: Assume 12 primary breaches per p.62 Appendix C detailed analysis governs, with 13th item being ACSR core itself counted separately in task summary; reason - CSB forensic count (p.62) is more specific than synopsis, and ACSR is initial failure point distinct from subsequent 12 breaches.

rfi.issue: Withheld Section 4.0/4.1 exact initial breach location within ACSR core (which pass, layer, header, nozzle)
rfi.reason: Needed to link thermal-fatigue evidence to sudden rupture path; withheld clauses prevent citing exact CSB conclusion
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION with reason: Assume initial breach originated in ACSR core involving B-pass / adjacent parting-sheet/fin joints where cyclic boiling instability and prior repairs concentrate; reason - p.34 B-pass instability mechanism + p.61 simultaneous A+B dP loss indicating core breach + p.22 thermal fatigue at several locations + p.66 most-repaired exchanger.

rfi.issue: Exact DCS values (pressures, stream/metal temperatures, dP) at 10:50 p.m.-11:24 p.m. not legible in available pages (Fig.42 trends only)
rfi.item: Time-series values for ACSR/AWSR T and dP on night of incident
rfi.reason: Needed to quantify curtailment transient ROC and confirm no alarm vs actual excursion
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION with reason: Assume curtailment transient imposed rapid cooldown/boiling-regime shift exceeding 3.6 degF/min start-up/shutdown and 1.8 degF/min normal limits (p.32/p.36), consistent with p.37-38 history of routine exceedances; reason - p.61 A-pass dP drop from 10:50 p.m. and p.33-34 upset description, to be verified by DCS export in test plan.

rfi.issue: Metal vs fluid ROC ratio conflict on p.38 (10x vs 4x less) and truncated exceedance % sentence
rfi.item: True metal-temperature ROC vs stream ROC attenuation and % time exceeded
rfi.reason: Determines whether metal-sensor monitoring alone is adequate for integrity operating window
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION with reason: Assume metal ROC significantly damps fluid ROC (factor ~4-10x) but still exceeded limits 2-3% of run time in 2011 (p.38); reason - both statements on same page indicate damping yet persistent exceedance, conservative to assume worst-case fluid ROC governs fatigue.

rfi.issue: Table 8 ambiguity: Documentation does not state which crack resulted in the leak that needed repair (early ACSR campaigns)
rfi.item: Which of repairs 1-7 were LOC vs benign cracks
rfi.reason: Affects crack-growth-rate and leak-before-break history interpretation
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION with reason: Assume at least one LOC per campaign (2007, 2011, 2014, 2015) as table lists LOC per group; reason - p.67 explicitly groups LOC per date and p.66 totals multiple LOCs, conservative for LBB invalidation.

rfi.issue: Vent-hole status of 2015 ACSR blocked-pass repair (sealed weld vs silicone-vented) not stated
rfi.item: Whether blocked B-pass vents were sealed shut
rfi.reason: Sealed blocked layer can pressure up if adjacent pass leaks internally, adding burst risk beyond thermal fatigue
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION with reason: Assume 2015 repair left vent holes sealed (PGP practice per p.45); reason - p.45 states PGP is facility using sealed holes and silicone practice described as other/recent, not PGP.

rfi.issue: BAHX internal design details withheld: dummy / inactive layers, pass numbering, design pressure/temperature, manufacturer (Chart vs Linde) selected for ACSR
rfi.item: ACSR nameplate design conditions and internal layer arrangement
rfi.reason: Needed to assess fitness-for-service and whether replacement design reduced thermal stress
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION with reason: Assume ACSR is Chart-type aluminum core without effective dummy-layer thermal buffer and rated for cryogenic service below -50 degF (p.12) with ~-90 degF turboexpander feed (p.59); reason - p.42 Chart-dummy-layer debate and cryogenic definition bound the service, to be verified by nameplate/U-stamp.

rfi.issue: Time-base misalignment: CSB states time stamps from sources did not match, used instrument signals and visual clues to determine relative shifts (p.60)
rfi.item: Absolute vs relative timing of DCS, event log, surveillance video
rfi.reason: Sequence (ACSR before AWSR) depends on corrected alignment
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION with reason: Assume relative sequence in p.61 (ACSR metal/dP loss 11:20-11:22 before AWSR 11:22-11:25) is correct after CSB alignment; reason - CSB explicitly reconciled shifts and sequence is corroborated by video fire-intensification (p.62).

test_plan.acceptance: Match CSB-corrected timeline within +/-60 s and confirm ACSR precedes AWSR; if AWSR precedes, reopen initial-point hypothesis
test_plan.closes_rfi: Absolute vs relative timing; DCS values night of incident
test_plan.measurements: Export raw DCS historian (1-s), event log, PLC clocks, surveillance DVR timestamps; record sensor tag list for Fig.42 metal-T and A/B dP
test_plan.procedure: At control room/historian: pull 10:30 p.m.-11:30 p.m. June 27 trends for ACSR/AWSR; photograph clock offsets; cross-correlate video flash frame to dP drop; re-plot Fig.42 with raw values
test_plan.purpose: Verify curtailment transient ROC and failure sequence
test_plan.test: T-01 DCS and video time-alignment audit

test_plan.acceptance: Calculate per-minute ROC for each stream and metal tag; exceedance of 3.6 degF/min (transient) or 1.8 degF/min (steady) flags integrity-window violation
test_plan.closes_rfi: Metal vs fluid ROC ratio; night-of-incident ROC
test_plan.measurements: Inlet, outlet, and external metal temperatures on ACSR/AWSR at >=1/min resolution, Jan 2011-June 2016 plus night of incident
test_plan.procedure: Compute ROC histograms per Fig.28/29 bins (1.8-3.6, 3.6-12.6, 12.6-21.6, 21.6-30.6, >30.6 degF/min); normalize to A-Train run time; compare metal vs fluid attenuation
test_plan.purpose: Quantify thermal-fatigue loading vs ALPEMA/Chart/GPA/API 662 limits

test_plan.acceptance: Document all 12 (or 13) breaches with photos, P&ID mark-up, and failure-mode label (ductile rupture vs fire damage vs fatigue origin); reconcile count
test_plan.closes_rfi: Breach count conflict; ACSR origin layer/pass
test_plan.measurements: Visual + dye-penetrant of ACSR core exterior, headers, nozzles, side/cap sheets; map each breach location and fracture surface
test_plan.procedure: Walk A-Train cryogenic area with P&IDs: tag each breach 1-13, photograph fracture faces before cleaning, retain coupons for SEM; distinguish primary fatigue rupture from secondary fire/overpressure tears
test_plan.purpose: Confirm ACSR as initial point and progression
test_plan.test: T-03 Field breach inventory and fractography triage

test_plan.acceptance: UT thickness / phased-array indication of disbonds or cracks > acceptance per owner spec; any internal crack in blocked-pass wall fails
test_plan.measurements: NDE of ACSR remnant and sister exchangers (B-cold, A/B-warm): external PT, UT shear-wave of side/cap sheets, borescope of blocked passes 97-99 type and ACSR pass 10 sealing
test_plan.procedure: At laydown/cold box: PT all prior weld repairs (Fig.49-52 locations), UT around attachment plates, verify vent holes sealed vs silicone-vented by pick test and pressure vent check; record nameplate, U-stamp, dummy-layer drawings
test_plan.purpose: Assess repair quality and trapped-fluid risk
test_plan.test: T-04 NDE of repairs and blocked-pass vents

test_plan.acceptance: If internal leak rate >0 or blocked-layer pressure rises on N2 test, blocked-pass containment is compromised - requires replacement not re-weld
test_plan.closes_rfi: Which cracks were LOC; LBB validity
test_plan.measurements: Helium/N2 pressure-hold and leak rate of each pass on spare/sister BAHX; sniff for interpass leakage
test_plan.procedure: Isolate passes, pressurize one pass to operating dP, monitor adjacent/blocked pass pressure for 4 h; use mass-spec leak detection at cap/side-bar welds
test_plan.purpose: Test LBB assumption that leaks are detectable/benign

test_plan.acceptance: Obtain P&ID-verified lineup: slug catcher -> dehydrator/dust collector -> warm separator -> turboexpander (-90F) / JT -> cold separator -> demethanizer with ACSR/AWSR reboiling -> NGL bullets -> Tri-States; residue -> Destin; condensate -> truck
test_plan.measurements: P&ID walkdown, valve lineup for A-Train curtailment/shut-in procedure actually used at 10:50-11:22 p.m., storage-bullet levels
test_plan.procedure: Field verify each unit on path, photograph nameplates, interview board/outside operators on curtailment steps; copy operating procedure and DCS set-point changes
test_plan.purpose: Define system boundary for PHA/MOC review

units_on_path: Offshore feed - Destin pipeline (raw gas from Gulf of Mexico deepwater)
Slug catcher (condensate collection; condensate trucked offsite)
Warm separator (liquids to demethanizer bottom; vapor splits to 3 streams)
Turboexpander (refrigeration to about -90 degF) + parallel JT/expander paths
A-Train cold side reboiler ACSR - BAHX (suspected initial failure point)
A-Train warm side reboiler AWSR - BAHX
B-Train cold side + warm side reboilers - BAHXs (sister units)
NGL product - onsite storage bullets (limited surge) -> Tri-States pipeline (curtailed downstream cause)
Flare / atmospheric vent (emergency fuel venting; let-burn philosophy)
